To find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y) \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\  & =4x\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+y{e}^{x}) \\  & =2x\cdot {y}^{2}+y\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =2x{y}^{2}+y{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2}+y{e}^{x}) \\  & =2x\cdot 2y+1\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =4xy+{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${f}_{xyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{xy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4xy+{e}^{x}) \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot y+{e}^{x} \\  & =4y+{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)) \\  & =x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ and ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})+\frac{\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})=\sqrt{3}-\frac{\pi }{6} \\ {g}_{yy}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})=-\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
{g}_{xx}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3})-{g}_{yy}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3})=\sqrt{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}-(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\sqrt{3}.
$$
